messages.author: 6db3c86d422c5ae9
messages.subject: Calculate correlation between latent factors
parts:
Hello lavaan group,

I am calculating the correlation between latent variables in my model. To do this I set the factor variances to one. By doing that way I guess I will obtain correlations among the latent variables rather than covariances among them.

My model is following:

fit <- cfa(mymodel, data = myData, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit, standardized = T)

As a result, the correlation coefficients will be presented in the column "Std.all" of the section "Covariance". Is it correct?

Thank you very much,
Kind regards,
Torres

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Calculate correlation between latent factors
parts: As a result, the correlation coefficients will be presented in the column "Std.all" of the section "Covariance". Is it correct?

That would be the case even if you set std.lv = FALSE.  If you fix the factor variances to 1, then the covariances in the unstandardized solution ("Estimate" column) are by definition correlations.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
